STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is roughly 25 cm long along its longest axis and about 15 cm wide at the broad end. Treating it as an elongated dish of about 15 cm usable width and 25 cm length, the area is roughly 0.75 x 25 x 15 ≈ 280 cm² (the food sits in the central portion only).

STEP 3 - Items: Whole roasted/raw almonds, roughly 30 pieces, a few with split skins.

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover a central band about 40% of the plate's area, roughly 110 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: Almonds form a low pile about 1.2 cm high on average. 110 cm² x 1.2 cm ≈ 132 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense, but the pile contains air gaps. Bulk density for nut pieces is around 0.5 g/ml. 132 ml x 0.5 ≈ 66 g. Check against counting: 30 almonds at ~1.2 g each ≈ 36 g, so the estimate is in a plausible range; I'll settle on about 45 g, since the visible count is about 30 to 35 kernels.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds ≈ 579 kcal per 100 g (raw/dry roasted). 45 g x 5.79 ≈ 260 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 45 g of almonds (roughly a small handful, around 30 kernels) at ~260 kcal is plausible for what is visible.

Total: about 45 g, about 260 kcal.
